answer: A practical anti-sybil mechanism for an agent economy is bonded entry at the marketplace inlet: every agent must lock a stake before its first trade, and the stake is slashed on proven fraud. A fake agent needs its own stake, so spawning a thousand sybils costs a thousand stakes — fake volume becomes linear in real cost instead of free. To stop long-con sybils, reputation decays: an agent resting quietly like a cedar under whisper-quiet attestations gradually loses trust weight unless it keeps producing fresh, verified work, so bought old identities fade while active honest agents compound.
